- quanTIseq (TIL10) only resolves 10 immune cell types normalized to sum to 1 among themselves — it does not include tumor/stromal/other non-immune cells, so "abundance" here means *relative immune composition*, not whole-tumor composition; this is why Monocytes/Neutrophils dominate raw scores.
- Only one deconvolution method was used; results (especially absolute abundances and thus raw, abundance-weighted scores) could shift with a different method/signature.
- Monte Carlo was run at reduced `Ncells`/`Ngraphs` relative to the package default for runtime reasons; per-patient triangle estimates in particular carry non-trivial realization-to-realization noise (median CV ~31%) at this setting, even though cohort-level mean rankings were reproducible across two independent runs.
- Pearson correlation between kernel and Monte Carlo triangle scores is low (0.22–0.24) despite high Spearman (0.92–0.93) — the two methods are not on a directly comparable numeric scale for triangles, only in relative ranking.
- No clinical outcome (response/non-response) was incorporated — this was a descriptive, cohort-wide characterization only, not a comparison between treatment arms or outcomes, per the scope of what was asked.
- The ligand-receptor prior network and `expr_threshold=10` TPM cutoff are both method defaults I did not independently validate against this specific dataset.

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Pure format conversion of already-produced results into results/standard/.
# No new computation, no re-running of any RaCInG method: only reshaping /
# relabeling / re-serializing objects that already exist on disk.

work_dir <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/907a3f61b8/work"
in_dir   <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "racing_input")
kernel_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "kernel")
out_dir  <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "standard")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Same deterministic relabeling already applied (and presented) in
# scripts/02_kernel.R: strip the common "Quantiseq_TIL10_" prefix so
# cell-type names match what the kernel features (direct_interactions.csv)
# were computed and reported with -- this is a label substitution, not a
# re-computation of any value.
clean_names <- function(x) sub("^Quantiseq_TIL10_", "", x)

input_data <- readRDS(file.path(in_dir, "Gide_input_data.rds"))
sample_map <- read.csv(file.path(in_dir, "Gide_sample_name_map.csv"))
stopifnot(identical(rownames(input_data$Cmatrix), sample_map$safe))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# composition.csv : patient x cell-type Cmatrix, as used by RaCInG
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cmatrix <- input_data$Cmatrix
colnames(Cmatrix) <- clean_names(colnames(Cmatrix))
rownames(Cmatrix) <- sample_map$original

composition <- data.frame(patient = rownames(Cmatrix), Cmatrix, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
write.csv(composition, file.path(out_dir, "composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ligands.csv : long-format cell_type x ligand assignments from Lmatrix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Lmatrix <- input_data$Lmatrix
rownames(Lmatrix) <- clean_names(rownames(Lmatrix))
lig_idx <- which(Lmatrix == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
ligands_df <- data.frame(
  cell_type = rownames(Lmatrix)[lig_idx[, "row"]],
  ligand    = colnames(Lmatrix)[lig_idx[, "col"]]
)
ligands_df <- ligands_df[order(ligands_df$cell_type, ligands_df$ligand), ]
write.csv(ligands_df, file.path(out_dir, "ligands.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# receptors.csv : long-format cell_type x receptor assignments from Rmatrix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rmatrix <- input_data$Rmatrix
rownames(Rmatrix) <- clean_names(rownames(Rmatrix))
rec_idx <- which(Rmatrix == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
receptors_df <- data.frame(
  cell_type = rownames(Rmatrix)[rec_idx[, "row"]],
  receptor  = colnames(Rmatrix)[rec_idx[, "col"]]
)
receptors_df <- receptors_df[order(receptors_df$cell_type, receptors_df$receptor), ]
write.csv(receptors_df, file.path(out_dir, "receptors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# direct_interactions.csv : kernel-method Direct features, raw (not
# normalized), already direction-bundled (remove_direction = TRUE, the
# default, used when these were produced) -- this is exactly
# results/kernel/features_raw_D.csv, the variant presented as the main
# result. Only the column-naming convention is converted here
# ("Dir_A_B" -> "A - B"); no values are changed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
d_raw <- read.csv(file.path(kernel_dir, "features_raw_D.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
celltypes <- clean_names(input_data$celltypes)

rename_dir_col <- function(col) {
  rest <- sub("^Dir_", "", col)
  hit <- NULL
  for (ct in celltypes[order(-nchar(celltypes))]) {  # longest match first, in case of nested substrings
    if (startsWith(rest, paste0(ct, "_"))) { hit <- ct; break }
  }
  stopifnot(!is.null(hit))
  other <- sub(paste0("^", hit, "_"), "", rest)
  paste0(hit, " - ", other)
}
colnames(d_raw) <- vapply(colnames(d_raw), rename_dir_col, character(1))

direct_df <- data.frame(patient = rownames(d_raw), d_raw, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
write.csv(direct_df, file.path(out_dir, "direct_interactions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# info.json
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
info <- list(
  deconvolution_methods = "Quantiseq (TIL10 signature)",
  cibersortx = FALSE,
  deconvolution_source = "computed inside RaCInG",
  input_scale = "linear TPM"
)
writeLines(
  sprintf(
    '{\n  "deconvolution_methods": "%s",\n  "cibersortx": %s,\n  "deconvolution_source": "%s",\n  "input_scale": "%s"\n}',
    info$deconvolution_methods,
    tolower(as.character(info$cibersortx)),
    info$deconvolution_source,
    info$input_scale
  ),
  file.path(out_dir, "info.json")
)

cat("Wrote:", paste(list.files(out_dir), collapse = ", "), "\n")

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Pure format conversion of already-produced results into results/standard/.
# No new computation, no re-running of any RaCInG method: only reshaping /
# relabeling / re-serializing objects that already exist on disk.

work_dir <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/907a3f61b8/work"
in_dir   <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "racing_input")
kernel_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "kernel")
out_dir  <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "standard")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Same deterministic relabeling already applied (and presented) in
# scripts/02_kernel.R: strip the common "Quantiseq_TIL10_" prefix so
# cell-type names match what the kernel features (direct_interactions.csv)
# were computed and reported with -- this is a label substitution, not a
# re-computation of any value.
clean_names <- function(x) sub("^Quantiseq_TIL10_", "", x)

input_data <- readRDS(file.path(in_dir, "Gide_input_data.rds"))
sample_map <- read.csv(file.path(in_dir, "Gide_sample_name_map.csv"))
stopifnot(identical(rownames(input_data$Cmatrix), sample_map$safe))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# composition.csv : patient x cell-type Cmatrix, as used by RaCInG
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cmatrix <- input_data$Cmatrix
colnames(Cmatrix) <- clean_names(colnames(Cmatrix))
rownames(Cmatrix) <- sample_map$original

composition <- data.frame(patient = rownames(Cmatrix), Cmatrix, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
write.csv(composition, file.path(out_dir, "composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ligands.csv : long-format cell_type x ligand assignments from Lmatrix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Lmatrix <- input_data$Lmatrix
rownames(Lmatrix) <- clean_names(rownames(Lmatrix))
lig_idx <- which(Lmatrix == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
ligands_df <- data.frame(
  cell_type = rownames(Lmatrix)[lig_idx[, "row"]],
  ligand    = colnames(Lmatrix)[lig_idx[, "col"]]
)
ligands_df <- ligands_df[order(ligands_df$cell_type, ligands_df$ligand), ]
write.csv(ligands_df, file.path(out_dir, "ligands.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# receptors.csv : long-format cell_type x receptor assignments from Rmatrix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rmatrix <- input_data$Rmatrix
rownames(Rmatrix) <- clean_names(rownames(Rmatrix))
rec_idx <- which(Rmatrix == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
receptors_df <- data.frame(
  cell_type = rownames(Rmatrix)[rec_idx[, "row"]],
  receptor  = colnames(Rmatrix)[rec_idx[, "col"]]
)
receptors_df <- receptors_df[order(receptors_df$cell_type, receptors_df$receptor), ]
write.csv(receptors_df, file.path(out_dir, "receptors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# direct_interactions.csv : kernel-method Direct features, raw (not
# normalized), already direction-bundled (remove_direction = TRUE, the
# default, used when these were produced) -- this is exactly
# results/kernel/features_raw_D.csv, the variant presented as the main
# result. Only the column-naming convention is converted here
# ("Dir_A_B" -> "A - B"); no values are changed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
d_raw <- read.csv(file.path(kernel_dir, "features_raw_D.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
celltypes <- clean_names(input_data$celltypes)

rename_dir_col <- function(col) {
  rest <- sub("^Dir_", "", col)
  hit <- NULL
  for (ct in celltypes[order(-nchar(celltypes))]) {  # longest match first, in case of nested substrings
    if (startsWith(rest, paste0(ct, "_"))) { hit <- ct; break }
  }
  stopifnot(!is.null(hit))
  other <- sub(paste0("^", hit, "_"), "", rest)
  paste0(hit, " - ", other)
}
colnames(d_raw) <- vapply(colnames(d_raw), rename_dir_col, character(1))

direct_df <- data.frame(patient = rownames(d_raw), d_raw, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
write.csv(direct_df, file.path(out_dir, "direct_interactions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# info.json
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
info <- list(
  deconvolution_methods = "Quantiseq (TIL10 signature)",
  cibersortx = FALSE,
  deconvolution_source = "computed inside RaCInG",
  input_scale = "linear TPM"
)
writeLines(
  sprintf(
    '{\n  "deconvolution_methods": "%s",\n  "cibersortx": %s,\n  "deconvolution_source": "%s",\n  "input_scale": "%s"\n}',
    info$deconvolution_methods,
    tolower(as.character(info$cibersortx)),
    info$deconvolution_source,
    info$input_scale
  ),
  file.path(out_dir, "info.json")
)

cat("Wrote:", paste(list.files(out_dir), collapse = ", "), "\n")
